meta.description: Batch program that generates a formatted transaction detail report for credit card transactions within a specified date range, with subtotals by card account and grand totals.
meta.process_description: The program reads a date parameter file to establish a reporting period (start date and end date), then sequentially reads all credit card transactions, filtering only those processed within that date range. For each qualifying transaction, it enriches the transaction data by looking up the card-to-account cross-reference, the transaction type description, and the transaction category description, then prints a formatted detail line on the report. The report is organised by card number, printing account-level subtotals whenever the card number changes, page-level subtotals every 20 lines with column headers repeated, and a grand total at the end of the report.

files.TRANFILE: Sequential input file containing posted credit card transactions to be reported on
files.CARDXREF: Card-to-account cross-reference index used to resolve a card number to its associated customer account
files.TRANTYPE: Reference index containing transaction type codes and their business descriptions (e.g. Purchase, Payment)
files.TRANCATG: Reference index containing transaction category codes and their business descriptions (e.g. Groceries, Travel) keyed by type and category code
files.TRANREPT: Sequential output file receiving the formatted transaction detail report
files.DATEPARM: Input parameter file specifying the start and end dates that define the reporting period

business_rules: Only transactions whose processing date falls within the configured start date and end date (inclusive) are included in the report; transactions outside this range are silently skipped.
Transactions are grouped by card number; an account subtotal line is printed whenever the card number changes between consecutive transactions.
A page break with column headers reprinted is triggered every 20 detail lines to maintain report readability.
Each transaction line is enriched with a human-readable transaction type description and transaction category description sourced from reference tables, rather than displaying raw codes.
The card number is resolved to a customer account via the card cross-reference file, associating each transaction with the correct account on the report.
Page totals are accumulated into the grand total when a page break occurs, ensuring the grand total at the end of the report reflects all transactions in the reporting period.
The reporting period is driven entirely by an external date parameter file, making the report reusable for any date range without program changes.
The program abends (abnormal termination) if any reference file or the transaction file returns an unexpected I/O error, ensuring report integrity is not compromised by missing or corrupt data.

Inserts the two-digit standard file status code into the last two positions of the display code, producing a consistently formatted four-digit error reference.
Prints the formatted standard file status code to the operator console or job log for error diagnosis and incident reporting.
Closes the conditional logic block that distinguishes between system-level binary errors and standard file status errors.
Marks the end of the error display routine and returns control to the calling paragraph so the program can proceed with its abend or recovery logic.

variables.name: FD-TRANFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for a single posted credit card transaction read from the transaction input file. Each occurrence represents one financial transaction to be evaluated for inclusion in the report.

variables.name: FD-TRANS-DATA
variables.description: The core transaction payload (transaction ID, type, category, source, description, amount, merchant details, card number, and origination timestamp) read directly from the transaction file before being mapped into the structured TRAN-RECORD working-storage layout for processing.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-PROC-TS
variables.description: The processing timestamp of the transaction as stored in the transaction file. This is the key date/time value used to determine whether the transaction falls within the configured reporting period start and end dates; transactions outside the range are excluded from the report.

variables.name: FD-FILLER
variables.description: Unused padding bytes at the end of the transaction file record, ensuring the physical record length matches the defined 350-byte transaction record layout. Has no business meaning.

variables.name: FD-CARDXREF-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for a single entry in the card-to-account cross-reference index. Used to resolve a card number found on a transaction to the customer account that should appear on the report.

variables.name: FD-XREF-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The credit card number that serves as the lookup key when reading the card cross-reference index. The program uses the card number from each transaction to find the corresponding customer account ID to display on the report.

variables.name: FD-XREF-DATA
variables.description: The remaining cross-reference record data (customer ID and account ID) returned after a card number lookup. This data is mapped into the CARD-XREF-RECORD working-storage structure to extract the account ID for display on the transaction report line.

variables.name: FD-TRANTYPE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for a single entry in the transaction type reference index. Used to retrieve the human-readable description of a transaction type code (e.g. 'Purchase', 'Payment') to enrich each report line.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-TYPE
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code that acts as the lookup key into the transaction type reference index (e.g. 'PR' for Purchase, 'PA' for Payment). Matched against the type code on each transaction to retrieve its business description.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-DATA
variables.description: The remainder of the transaction type reference record (type description and filler) returned after a type code lookup. Mapped into the TRAN-TYPE-RECORD working-storage structure to extract the readable type description for printing on the report.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-RECORD
variables.description: File buffer record for a single entry in the transaction category reference index. Used to retrieve the human-readable description of a transaction category (e.g. 'Groceries', 'Travel') keyed by the combination of transaction type and category code.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY
variables.description: The composite lookup key used to retrieve a transaction category description from the category reference index, combining the transaction type code and category code to uniquely identify the category within a given transaction type.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-TYPE-CD
variables.description: The two-character transaction type code forming the first part of the composite category lookup key. Together with the category code, it uniquely identifies the business category description to display on the report (e.g. type 'PR' + category '0001' = 'Groceries').

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-CD
variables.description: The four-digit numeric transaction category code forming the second part of the composite category lookup key. Combined with the type code, it pinpoints the specific spending category (e.g. groceries, travel, dining) whose description will be printed on the report line.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-DATA
variables.description: The remainder of the transaction category reference record (category description and filler) returned after a category lookup. Mapped into the TRAN-CAT-RECORD working-storage structure to extract the readable category description for printing on the report.

variables.name: FD-REPTFILE-REC
variables.description: Output buffer for a single 133-character line written to the transaction detail report file. Every formatted report line — whether a header, transaction detail, subtotal, page total, or grand total — is placed here before being written to the report output.

variables.name: FD-DATEPARM-REC
variables.description: Input buffer for the date parameter record read from the external date parameter file. Contains the start and end dates that define the reporting period, allowing the report to be run for any date range without changing the program.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned by the operating system after each read operation on the transaction input file. Used to detect end-of-file (normal completion) or unexpected errors that would compromise report integrity and trigger an abend.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the transaction file I/O status code. A value of '0' indicates a successful operation; '1' signals end-of-file, meaning all transactions have been read; any other value indicates an error requiring an abend.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the transaction file I/O status code, providing additional detail about the specific I/O condition encountered. Used together with TRANFILE-STAT1 to diagnose and handle file errors precisely.

variables.name: CARDXREF-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each lookup against the card cross-reference index. Used to confirm that a card number was successfully resolved to an account, or to detect missing records and I/O errors that would require an abend.

variables.name: CARDXREF-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the card cross-reference I/O status. A value of '0' means the card number was found and the account resolved successfully; any other value signals a lookup failure or I/O error.

variables.name: CARDXREF-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the card cross-reference I/O status, providing granular detail about the specific outcome of the card-to-account lookup operation.

variables.name: TRANTYPE-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each lookup against the transaction type reference index. Used to verify that a valid, human-readable type description was retrieved for each transaction, or to detect errors requiring an abend.

variables.name: TRANTYPE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the transaction type reference I/O status. Confirms whether the type code lookup succeeded ('0') or encountered a missing record or file error.

variables.name: TRANTYPE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the transaction type reference I/O status, providing additional diagnostic detail about the type code lookup result.

variables.name: TRANCATG-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each lookup against the transaction category reference index. Used to confirm that a valid spending category description was retrieved, or to detect errors that would compromise report accuracy.

variables.name: TRANCATG-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the transaction category reference I/O status. A value of '0' confirms the category description was found; other values indicate a missing category or file error requiring an abend.

variables.name: TRANCATG-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the transaction category reference I/O status, providing granular detail about the specific outcome of the category lookup.

variables.name: TRANREPT-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after each write operation to the transaction detail report output file. Used to confirm that each report line was written successfully, or to detect output errors that would result in an incomplete or corrupt report.

variables.name: REPTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the report output file I/O status. A value of '0' confirms the report line was written successfully; any other value signals a write failure requiring an abend to protect report integrity.

variables.name: REPTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the report output file I/O status, providing additional detail about the specific write outcome for diagnostic purposes.

variables.name: DATEPARM-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character I/O status code returned after reading the date parameter file. Used to confirm that the reporting period start and end dates were successfully loaded, without which no transactions can be correctly filtered.

variables.name: DATEPARM-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the date parameter file I/O status. A value of '0' confirms the reporting period dates were read successfully; any other value indicates the parameter file is missing or unreadable, making the report impossible to produce.

variables.name: DATEPARM-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the date parameter file I/O status, providing granular detail about the specific read outcome for the reporting period parameter file.

variables.name: WS-DATEPARM-RECORD
variables.description: Working-storage representation of the date parameter record loaded from the external parameter file. Holds the start and end dates that define the reporting period, used to filter which transactions are included in the report.

variables.name: WS-START-DATE
variables.description: The earliest date of the reporting period. Only transactions whose processing timestamp falls on or after this date are included in the report. Sourced from the external date parameter file, making the report reusable for any date range.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A single separator character (likely a space or delimiter) between the start and end dates in the date parameter record. Has no business meaning; purely a formatting artifact of the parameter file layout.

variables.name: WS-END-DATE
variables.description: The latest date of the reporting period. Only transactions whose processing timestamp falls on or before this date are included in the report. Together with WS-START-DATE, it defines the inclusive date window for the transaction detail report.

variables.name: WS-REPORT-VARS
variables.description: Collection of working-storage control and accumulator variables that govern report formatting, pagination, and financial totalling throughout the batch report generation process.

variables.name: WS-FIRST-TIME
variables.description: A flag that indicates whether the report has been initialised yet. Set to 'Y' at the start; when the first qualifying transaction is encountered, the report headers are printed and this flag is cleared, preventing duplicate header printing on subsequent transactions.

variables.name: WS-LINE-COUNTER
variables.description: Tracks how many transaction detail lines have been printed on the current report page. When this counter reaches the page size limit (20 lines), a page break is triggered, column headers are reprinted, and the counter resets to maintain a readable, consistently formatted report.

variables.name: WS-PAGE-SIZE
variables.description: The maximum number of transaction detail lines allowed per report page before a page break occurs. Set to 20, this controls the physical layout of the printed report, ensuring each page is consistently sized and easy to read.

variables.name: WS-BLANK-LINE
variables.description: A pre-initialised blank line of 133 spaces used to insert visual spacing between sections of the report (e.g. between account groups or before totals), improving the readability of the printed output.

variables.name: WS-PAGE-TOTAL
variables.description: Running sum of transaction amounts for the current report page. Accumulated as each transaction is printed and rolled into the grand total when a page break occurs, ensuring the grand total correctly reflects all transactions across all pages.

variables.name: WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL
variables.description: Running sum of transaction amounts for the current card account being processed. Printed as an account subtotal line whenever the card number changes between consecutive transactions, giving a per-account financial summary on the report.

variables.name: WS-GRAND-TOTAL
variables.description: Cumulative sum of all transaction amounts across every account and every page in the report. Printed as the final grand total line at the end of the report, representing the total financial activity for the entire reporting period.

variables.name: WS-CURR-CARD-NUM
variables.description: Holds the card number of the transaction currently being processed. Compared against the card number of each new transaction to detect when the account group changes, triggering the printing of an account subtotal line before starting the next account's transactions.

variables.name: IO-STATUS
variables.description: General-purpose two-character I/O status work area used to capture and evaluate file operation results across multiple files, supporting centralised error checking logic in the program.

variables.name: IO-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the general I/O status code. The primary indicator of whether a file operation succeeded ('0'), reached end-of-file ('1'), or encountered an error requiring an abend.

variables.name: IO-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the general I/O status code, providing supplementary detail about the specific file operation outcome for error diagnosis.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-BINARY
variables.description: A two-byte binary numeric work area used to interpret raw I/O status codes as a numeric value, enabling precise comparison and evaluation of file status conditions during error handling.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-ALPHA
variables.description: An alphanumeric overlay of the TWO-BYTES-BINARY field, allowing the same two bytes to be examined as individual characters. This enables the program to inspect each byte of an I/O status code separately for detailed error condition checking.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-LEFT
variables.description: The left (first) byte of the two-byte I/O status overlay, corresponding to the primary status character that indicates the general category of the file operation result (success, end-of-file, or error).

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
variables.description: The right (second) byte of the two-byte I/O status overlay, corresponding to the secondary status character that provides additional detail about the specific file operation outcome.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-04
variables.description: A structured work area used to decompose and store a numeric I/O status code into its component parts for detailed error reporting and abend diagnostics when a file operation fails.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0401
variables.description: The leading single digit of the decomposed I/O status code, representing the primary status category. Used in error messages to communicate the high-level nature of a file failure to operations staff.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0403
variables.description: The trailing three digits of the decomposed I/O status code, representing the specific error sub-code. Used alongside IO-STATUS-0401 in abend error messages to give operations staff precise information about which file operation failed and why.

variables.name: APPL-RESULT
variables.description: A signed numeric result code used to communicate the outcome of file operations and business logic checks. Acts as the program's internal pass/fail indicator; a value of 0 means the operation completed successfully, while any non-zero value signals a condition requiring error handling or an abend.

variables.name: APPL-AOK
variables.description: A condition name that evaluates to true when APPL-RESULT equals zero, meaning the most recent file or business operation completed without error. Used throughout the program to write readable conditional checks such as 'IF APPL-AOK' rather than comparing numeric codes directly.

variables.name: APPL-EOF
variables.description: Condition name that signals the transaction input file has been fully read — when the file system returns status code 16, all posted transactions have been processed and the program should stop reading and proceed to print final totals and close the report.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: Flag that tracks whether the transaction input file has been exhausted. Initialised to 'N' (not finished), it is set to indicate end-of-file once all transactions in the reporting period have been read, triggering the program to print the final account subtotal and grand total before closing the report.

variables.name: ABCODE
variables.description: Abnormal termination (abend) code passed to the system when the program encounters an unrecoverable error — such as an unexpected I/O failure on the transaction file or a reference table — ensuring operations teams can identify the exact failure reason and that a corrupt or incomplete report is never silently accepted.

variables.name: TIMING
variables.description: Numeric parameter passed to the system abend routine alongside the abend code, used to convey timing or context information about when the failure occurred during report generation, aiding in post-failure diagnosis and audit of the batch run.

paragraphs.name: 0550-DATEPARM-READ
paragraphs.description: This paragraph reads the reporting period configuration from the date parameter file, establishing the start and end dates that define which transactions will be included in the report. It handles all possible outcomes of that read operation, confirming success, detecting an empty file, or triggering an abnormal program termination if a data error occurs.

paragraphs.name: 1000-TRANFILE-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: Reads the next posted credit card transaction from the input file and determines whether processing should continue, end normally, or halt due to a data error. This paragraph acts as the controlled gateway for consuming each transaction record that will be evaluated against the reporting date range.

paragraphs.name: 1100-WRITE-TRANSACTION-REPORT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the writing of a single transaction detail line to the report, handling first-time report initialisation, page break management, and accumulation of running totals before printing the transaction. It ensures the report is properly structured with headers, page totals, and accurate financial summaries at every level.

paragraphs.name: 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph closes out the current report page by printing the accumulated page transaction total, rolling that total into the overall report grand total, resetting the page running total to zero, and reprinting the column headers ready for the next page of transactions.

paragraphs.name: 1120-WRITE-ACCOUNT-TOTALS
paragraphs.description: Closes out the current card account's section of the report by printing the accumulated subtotal for all transactions on that account, then resets the account running total to zero and reprints the column header row to clearly separate the next account's transactions.

paragraphs.name: 1110-WRITE-GRAND-TOTALS
paragraphs.description: Finalises the transaction detail report by writing the grand total line, which reflects the cumulative sum of all credit card transaction amounts processed across every account and page within the reporting period. This provides the auditable bottom-line figure for the entire report run.

paragraphs.name: 1120-WRITE-HEADERS
paragraphs.description: Prints the report page header section at the top of each new page, including the report title, a blank separator line, and two rows of column headings that label the transaction detail data below. This ensures every page of the report is clearly identified and the columns are consistently labelled for readability.

paragraphs.name: 1111-WRITE-REPORT-REC
paragraphs.description: This paragraph writes a single formatted line to the transaction detail report output file, and enforces report integrity by immediately halting the entire batch job if the write operation fails, preventing a corrupt or incomplete report from being produced.

paragraphs.name: 1120-WRITE-DETAIL
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and writes a single enriched transaction detail line to the report output file. It assembles all resolved business data — transaction identity, account, type, category, source, and amount — into a complete report record before printing it.

paragraphs.name: 0000-TRANFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the credit card transaction file in preparation for reading and reporting on posted transactions. It validates that the file is accessible and halts the entire report run with an error if the file cannot be opened, protecting report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 0100-REPTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the transaction detail report output file for writing, ensuring it is ready to receive formatted report content. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately halts with an error, preventing a corrupt or incomplete report from being produced.

paragraphs.name: 0200-CARDXREF-OPEN
paragraphs.description: Opens the card-to-account cross-reference file so the program can resolve card numbers to their associated customer accounts during report generation. If the file cannot be opened, the program abends immediately to prevent producing an incomplete or inaccurate report.

paragraphs.name: 0300-TRANTYPE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: Opens the transaction type reference table, which maps raw transaction type codes to human-readable descriptions (e.g. Purchase, Payment). If the file cannot be opened, the program abends immediately to prevent the report from being generated with missing or incomplete transaction descriptions.

paragraphs.name: 0400-TRANCATG-OPEN
paragraphs.description: Opens the transaction category reference table so the program can look up human-readable category descriptions (e.g. Groceries, Travel) for each transaction during report generation. If the file cannot be opened, the program abends immediately to prevent producing a report with missing or incomplete category information.

paragraphs.name: 0500-DATEPARM-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the date parameter file that defines the reporting period for the transaction report. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately abends to prevent a report being generated without valid start and end date boundaries.

paragraphs.name: 1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF
paragraphs.description: This paragraph resolves a credit card number to its associated customer account by looking up the card-to-account cross-reference file. If the card number cannot be found, the program logs an error and terminates abnormally to protect report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 1500-B-LOOKUP-TRANTYPE
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the human-readable description for a given transaction type code from the transaction type reference table, enabling the report to display meaningful labels such as 'Purchase' or 'Payment' instead of raw codes. If the transaction type code does not exist in the reference table, the program logs the unrecognised code and terminates abnormally to protect report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 1500-C-LOOKUP-TRANCATG
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the human-readable description for a transaction category (e.g. Groceries, Travel) from the category reference table, matching on the combined transaction type and category code. If no matching category is found, the program abends to protect report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9000-TRANFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the posted credit card transaction input file once all transactions have been processed. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program raises an error and terminates abnormally to protect report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9100-REPTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the transaction detail report output file after all report content has been written. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program abends to prevent a corrupt or incomplete report from being silently accepted.

paragraphs.name: 9200-CARDXREF-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the card-to-account cross-reference file once all transaction lookups are complete. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program raises an error and terminates abnormally to protect report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9300-TRANTYPE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Closes the transaction type reference file after all lookups are complete. Ensures the file is released cleanly, and abends the program if the closure fails to protect report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9400-TRANCATG-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Closes the transaction category reference file after all lookups are complete, ensuring the file is properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program abends to protect report integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9500-DATEPARM-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Closes the date parameter file after the reporting period boundaries have been read, ensuring the file resource is properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program abends to prevent silent data integrity issues.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs a controlled abnormal termination of the report generation program when an unrecoverable error is detected, ensuring the batch job fails visibly rather than producing an incomplete or corrupt transaction report.

paragraphs.name: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and displays a human-readable file status code whenever a file I/O error occurs, enabling operators and support staff to diagnose which file operation failed and why. It handles both standard numeric status codes and non-standard binary error codes returned by the operating system.
